conventions: In the border gazetteer, the lieth of a verbless relative clause with a prepositional predicate is the construction's linking verb under rules 20 and 49, not a supplied lexical verb under rule 20's added clause: it joins the preposition heading the predicate and the unit heads on that preposition. So מִנֶּגֶב → lieth on (18.13) and עַל־פְּנֵי → lieth before (18.14, 18.16), read exactly as the bare copula of בְּ → is in (18.16) and נֹכַח → is over against (18.17). Subtraction decides it: the Hebrew preposition has already made the locative predication, so what lieth adds is the link English writes for it, not a predication the Hebrew never wrote.

A compound cardinal whose two Hebrew morphemes the ASV writes as one English word is one fused unit under rule 30, and neither morpheme is unrepresented: שְׁתֵּים עֶשְׂרֵה → twelve (18.24) and אַרְבַּע עֶשְׂרֵה → fourteen (18.28). Head on the first numeral morpheme as rule 6's deterministic anchor, since the one English word writes no morpheme's lexeme in particular. Rule 42's count of waws against ands does not reach these: no waw stands between the two morphemes and no source item is coordinated.

מִן before a direction noun is read off the ASV and not off the lemma pair: מִצָּפוֹן → northward is one fused unit at 18.17 because a single English word carries both morphemes, while מִצָּפוֹן → on the north (18.12) and מִנֶּגֶב → on the south (18.5) are split, each morpheme holding a word of its own. The candidate table shows these in one bucket; they are rule 30's condition met and unmet, not a chapter split.
report: Read all 28 verses end to end against the 64-lemma candidate table and against the four `added` units, which the table cannot see. No construction is analysed two ways with nothing in the source or the ASV to license the difference, so there is nothing to patch.

Candidates checked and cleared: הַ on toponyms — the written for the Jordan and Manasseh chains (18.7, 12, 19, 20), no the written in the town list (18.23–26), which is rule 29's last sentence and not a split. לְ across ten treatments — dative left bare by an English indirect object (18.3, 7), recast as a possessive determiner (18.12, which is rule 41's own worked example), possessive have in a verbless clause (18.7) beside were on a present הָיָה (18.12, 21), and of / for / by / according to wherever the ASV writes a word. הַ → each at 18.4, with no אֶחָד in the phrase to claim it (rule 41). בֵּין at 18.11: the first takes between, the repeated one is unrepresented (rule 26). Directive he: takes to / at / unto where no preposition has already taken the relation (18.12, 13, 18), fuses with its host where the ASV writes one word (seven places), unrepresented where neither.

Two apparent table conflicts resolve as ASV-driven rather than as splits. מִן plus a direction noun fuses at 18.17 because the ASV writes the single word northward, and splits at 18.5 and 18.12 because it writes on the north / on the south — rule 30's one-rendering condition, decided by the English, and the 18.17 note already names the competing reading. פֵּאָה is the quarter or was the quarter according to whether the clause supplies a copula, and that copula is placed identically in every border formula (18.12, 14, 15, 19, 20).

The four added units were counted against the morphemes that could carry them, and the chapter folds supplied words in consistently everywhere else. yet (18.2) stands beside a negative already holding its own not; the description (18.6) is a supplied object noun that does not carry כָּתַב's lexeme (rule 44); thence (18.14) answers to no מִשָּׁם; and (18.28) stands between two names the Hebrew juxtaposes with no waw (rule 14's closing sentence). Against these, every other supplied word in the chapter has a morpheme that licenses it: supplied the on construct nouns (rule 29, 14 verses), supplied into / to / at only where no preposition is present (18.6, 9, 13, 16, 17), phrasal particles up, out, down, along, about, again with their verbs, and round about whole on סָבִיב (18.20).

BSB disagreements: none is a genuine error, and all fall in the documented convention classes. The five R rows are the object-marker-free dative of rules 40 and 27 and the repeated בֵּין of rule 26; the eight Td rows are 18.12's article whose determiner went to the suffix (rule 41's own example) and the town-list toponyms with no the written (rule 29); the two Sd rows are directive hes whose direction another morpheme or the construct relation has already taken (rule 32). The one worth naming is 18.7 לַ in מֵעֵבֶר לַיַּרְדֵּן → beyond: rule 40's closing test decides it, since the governed noun keeps the Jordan of its own, so only the relation is unstated and the preposition is unrepresented rather than drawn into the מֵעֵבֶר fusion.

Three conventions recorded: the linking-verb reading of lieth, the fused teens numerals, and the pointer explaining the מִן direction rows so a later reader does not reopen them. No promotions and no amendments: the lieth judgment is already decided by rule 20's sentence that the copula is whatever verb the ASV writes where a copula would stand, and the teens fusion is forced by rules 30 and 22 with no corpus precedent shown here to check a wider rule against.
